sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL4001.A21 P7 1991
sources.note: Glottolog attaches it to bori1243 but it describes Mising (misi1242, Assam). Ch.1 Phonology p.13: 28 phonemes, 3 suprasegmental (rising, falling, level tone); sec.1.4.3 pp.33-34 'three tones viz., high, level and low'. No word-stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence empty apart from tone description). Post 2015 says the tone report 'seems to be in error'.

sources.citation: Post, Mark W. 2015. Tones in Northeast Indian languages, with a focus on Tani: A fieldworker's guide. In Post, Morey & DeLancey (eds.), Language and Culture in Northeast India and Beyond (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 023), 182-211.
sources.note: p.190: 'Little or nothing is known about the remaining known Tani lects, i.e. Bokar-Ramo, Pailibo, Hill Miri, Bori, Aashing, Shimong and Damu.. the fact is that we do not know.' Table 5 p.190 lists Karko, Bori, Shimong under tone status 'Unknown' and Pasi-Padam (Pasighat) under 'No tone, confirmed'. Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Sun, Tianshin Jackson. 1993. A Historical-Comparative Study of the Tani (Mirish) Branch in Tibeto-Burman. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Bori appears only as lexical data ('Bori M' = Megu 1988, listed among supplementary sources p.10; 'Bori T'); no Bori phonological sketch. The only stress remarks are for Nishi (Chhangte data, App. II p.448: /ə/-/ɨ/ contrast neutralized in unstressed syllables) and a Benedict footnote on an unstressed *ʔa- prefix in Padam-Mising (p.52). Silent on Bori/Karko stress.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Bori (boj), source Megu 1988; Grambank bori1243 (sources Deb 1993 'Aspects of grammatical patterns of the Adi dialect', Lalrempuii 2005); Glottolog 5.3 bori1243 (Glottolog's most extensive descriptions Lalrempuii 2005, Prasad et al. 1991, Ouyang 1985, Barooah 1949, Duff-Sutherland-Dunbar 1915)
sources.note: WALS: Bori coded for 69A, 83A, 85A, 87A, 88A, 93A, 95A, 97A, 112A, 143A/E/F/G only; no stress features 14A-17A. Grambank and Glottolog: no phonological content; they only name the sources above.
